params: {via?: "online" (default: the open file is kept on the server in Preferences, `pref.publishServer`, and the server hands out the codes) | "local" (this app hosts it for people on the same network; no server), access?: "edit" (default) | "comment" (online only: view and comment, not edit) | "view" (online only: which code `code` is), server? (online: another server's address, with ?key=… when it needs its key), key? (online: the server's key, when the address has none), name? (online: the file's name there), port?, bind?: "lan" (default) | "local" (this machine only) | an IP address (local)} → the open file's session as `collab.peers` gives it: `code` is what others type to join (`collab.join {code}`, the Join field), `link` an invite link. Local: at once, the code carries the host's IPv4 address, port and secret (K7M2Q-…, 20 symbols). Online: status "connecting" first; once live `code` is the server's (K7M-2QX-9TD) and `share` is {via, access, shared, editCode, viewCode, commentCode, editLink, viewLink, commentLink}: links made for others (commentCode and commentLink null from a server older than comment links) (the file's own links in `published` stay yours); `code` stays null when the server is older than join codes (give `share.editLink` / `share.viewLink` instead). Called again while shared: only switches which code `code` is (`access`). Called after `collab.stop` on a file that is still on the server: new links and codes for that same file (nothing is published twice). `collab.stop` stops sharing

label: Stop live session
params: {} → {ended}: the open file's session ends (a session this app hosts stops for everyone; a joined one is left). A file shared online with `collab.share` is different: its sharing stops → {ended: false, shared: false}: the links and codes others got are revoked on the server, whoever joined with them is disconnected at once (they keep their copy), and you stay in the file, which stays on the server, open only to you (`collab.share` shares it again with new codes; `collab.leave` leaves it there; `collab.manageFile {action: "remove"}` with its owner token takes it off the server)

label: Join live session
params: {code | link (a join code: K7M-2QX-9TD from a server, asked at the server in Preferences; a longer one for the local network; spaces, dashes and case don't matter, O reads as 0 and I or L as 1; or an invite link: figcraft://join?host=…&file=…&token=…, figcraft://join?server=ws(s)://…&file=…&token=… or ws(s)://host:port/?file=…&token=…, from a session an app hosts or a server's share link; either key takes either)} → the new session: {session, status: "connecting", …}; its file opens in a tab of its own (other files' sessions go on) and `collab.peers` tells when it's live (`sessions` lists it until then, and if it fails)

label: Leave live session
params: {session? (a session's id from `collab.peers`'s `sessions`, e.g. a join still on its way; default: the open file's session)} → {ended}: the synced file stays open as a local copy

label: Publish to server
params: {server: ws://host:port/?key=… or wss://host/path/?key=… (the server's address with its key; `figcraft-server key` prints it; without a key on a server open to the public), key? (when the address has none), name? (default: the file's name)} → status "connecting": the open file is uploaded as a new file and this tab syncs through the server; `collab.peers` then has `published: {server, file, name, edit, view, owner (published without a key: the owner token, shown once), expires (seconds since 1970, or null)}` and `hosting` (the server's operator, terms and idle expiry)

label: Server info
params: {server: ws://host:port/ or wss://host/path/} → {open (anyone may publish without the key), operator, terms (a web address), idleDays (files published without the key are deleted after this many days unopened; null: kept), maxFileMb, expires}

params: {file (its id), server?, owner? (the server's address and the owner token you got when you published the file without the key; each defaults to what is recorded for one of your online files, see `collab.files`), action: links | createLink | revoke | share (others get new links and join codes) | unshare (the links and codes others got are revoked; the file stays yours on the server) | rename | remove (the file is deleted from the server and leaves your online files), access? (createLink: view (default) | comment | edit), label? (createLink), link? (revoke: a link's id), name? (rename)} → {links: [{id, access, label, created}]} | {id, access, link (a new share link, shown once)} | {shared, code, viewCode, commentCode, editLink, viewLink, commentLink} | {done}

params: {reason (a few words, at most 500 characters)} → {sent}: the file you joined on a server is reported to its operator; the session's message says when the server kept it (servers older than this app don't take reports)

label: People in this file
params: {} → the open file's session (each open file has its own or none): {available, canHost (false in the browser: it can only join), session (its id; null: this file isn't in a session), status: off|connecting|live|reconnecting|failed, reason?, role, me, name, color, fileName, pages, link, url, address, network, access: edit|view|comment (view: a server's view link, edits are refused; comment: its comment link, edits other than to comment threads are refused), readOnly (the open file can't be edited now: view only, comment only, or being published), published (a file you published: {server, file, name, edit, view}), code (the join code to give others, when the file was shared with `collab.share`; null otherwise or while it is on its way), share ({via: online|local, access, shared (false: a file of yours on a server that nobody else gets into now), editCode, viewCode, commentCode, editLink, viewLink, commentLink (what others join with; null when not shared)} or null), follow, syncing, document (index of the synced open document), editing (the text layer you type in: {node, layer, caret, selection}), peers: [{id, name, color, editing (theirs, same shape, or null), presence: {cursor: [page, x, y], selection, viewport: [page, x, y, w, h], editing_text}}], sessions: [{session, document (index of its open document; null for a join on its way), status, reason, role, fileName, link, peers (how many others)}] (every session of the app)}

Then: the server has everything in the copy → nothing more; the copy has changes of yours the server never confirmed and nothing else changed there → they are applied on top as one edit ("Recovered changes", synced to everyone); anything else changed meanwhile → the copy opens beside the file as “<name> (recovered copy)”; the file can't be joined → the copy opens as an unsaved document.
